## Recursive rules · Fibonacci {#ss1-recursive-rules .recursive-rules}

A recursive definition needs **starting values** and a rule using earlier terms.

For the sequence we found in OEIS, start with $a_1=1$ and $a_2=1$.

<div data-module="fibonacci" class="fibonacci-builder" aria-label="Build the Fibonacci sequence one term at a time"></div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 1 · Recursive rules · Next: Example 1.5</p>

::: notes
Return to the sequence students found in the opening OEIS investigation: 1,1,2,3,5,8,… . We use a_1=a_2=1 and the recurrence for n≥3.

Use Next term to reveal a term only after a prediction. Each calculation has four aligned lines: the general recurrence, substitution of the index, substitution of the two values, then the result. For a_4 these are a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}, a_4=a_3+a_2, a_4=2+1, a_4=3. Blue identifies the previous term throughout the working and term strip; orange identifies the term before it. The new term has a teal border. These roles update with each reveal.

Two or three reveals are sufficient. Reset restores only the starting values. Ask why both starting values are needed and what a_{n-1} and a_{n-2} mean.

In Example 1.5 only the immediately preceding term is used, with a multiplier depending on n. Source: https://oeis.org/A000045.
:::
